$comment: Project-specific exemptions for scripts/audit-ui.mjs. `allowedColourFiles` means "files that publish the rules": it exempts them from the colour rules and from `cardEyebrow`'s inline half, because a page that documents a treatment has to be able to show it. The rules live in the script and are shared; which files may break them is a property of this project. The allow-lists merge over the script's defaults, so an entry here only ever adds an exemption.

allowedColourFiles.app/foundations/page.tsx: The token reference. It prints every colour value in the theme by definition — a page that documents the palette has to contain the palette — so the colour rules cannot apply to it. This is the one file where a literal is the content rather than a decision, and it is why the exemption is scoped to this file alone rather than to `app/`.
allowedColourFiles.app/rules/page.tsx: The rule book. It publishes the semantic roles with their measured values and the contrast each one clears, which cannot be written without the values. Same reasoning as app/foundations/page.tsx.
allowedColourFiles.components/site/photo-stand-in.tsx: A stand-in for a photograph. The chip and overlay rules are about legibility on an arbitrary image, so their demos need a pale, busy surface the author does not control; a token-coloured gradient would be a background rather than a picture. This is the only file in the system that names palette colours, which is why it lives in the review site's own chrome rather than in the installed layer.
allowedColourFiles.components/mri/chips.tsx: The overlay scrims. A chip on a photograph is read against an image the author does not control, so the scrim cannot follow the theme: `bg-black/70` with `text-white` is ~8:1 against any picture, whereas a token scrim inverts with the theme and can land light-on-light. These five literals are absolute by design, they are the reason the overlay surface exists, and they are confined to the scrim constants at the top of this file.

tableAllowed.components/mri/patterns.tsx: TableSkeleton is the skeleton *for* a table, so it has to emit the real elements. It cannot use the shared composition: the whole point is to mirror the geometry of the table that will replace it without importing the data path behind it, and swapping in <Table> would make the skeleton depend on the thing it stands in for.
tableAllowed.components/mri/chip-audit.tsx: The chip audit is a specimen sheet. It prints a grid of every chip surface against every tone, which is a table of specimens rather than a data table, and it is installed as review chrome rather than as a page.

pageShellAllowed.components/site/site-footer.tsx: The shell chrome. The header and footer are the frame that PageContainer sits inside, not content within it, so they own their gutter and their width by construction. The same is true of the platform's components/shell/ footer, which is named in that project's config.
